text.content:
The most influential Ventrue — if not Kindred — of the ancient world, Camilla overthrew (or, by less charitable accounts, destroyed) his own sire Collat to seize Rome and guide the Ventrue through the Republic and into the Empire. Rather than ruling openly as a god-king, Camilla pioneered the Ventrue method of governing through mortal proxies: cultivating senators and officials with favors and information rather than crude domination, always keeping his own hand hidden. He created the first Ventrue council of peers, oversaw the destruction of Carthage in the Punic Wars, and presided over Rome and its Ventrue for nearly a thousand years before finally slipping into torpor.

Camilla has never been found since. Some prominent elders, including Robert Kross, actively search for him and his old confidant Lysander, believing that either could redirect the clan's fractured modern leadership. Rumor holds that one or both may already sit, unrevealed, upon the secretive Directorate.

A Greek Ventrue who fought (and hated) the Brujah of Athens during the Peloponnesian War, Lysander later became Camilla's most trusted agent, traveling the Mediterranean as Rome's eyes and, when needed, its sword. He personally took the last Brujah head during the razing of Carthage and, in later centuries, moved east with the fading Roman Empire to observe the rise of Byzantium. Some Ventrue credit him with guiding Hardestadt the Elder toward the founding of the Camarilla, though no confirmed sighting of Lysander has been recorded since. He is presumed to be either in torpor or working from deep concealment, possibly alongside Camilla.

Settling among the rustic Spartans centuries before their rise to power, this Ventrue took the guise of the goddess Artemis Orthia after being drawn into the philosopher Lycurgus' dream of a perfect warrior society. Having witnessed the mortal mob destroy her fellow Ventrue Medon (a self-declared god-king on the Aegean who demanded service and gave nothing in return), Artemis chose to work through mortal institutions rather than rule them directly — a lesson many Ventrue after her would emulate. She helped forge the Spartan-led Peloponnesian League and provoked the first war between Sparta and Brujah-influenced Athens. Torn apart by frenzied Brujah berserkers during the sack of Carthage in the Third Punic War, Artemis met her Final Death alongside the fall of the city she had spent centuries maneuvering to destroy.

A prominent Ventrue who survived the Inquisition's Nights of Fire relatively unscathed while many of his elders fell to the anarch revolt that followed, Hardestadt looked to Camilla and Artemis' histories of uniting Kindred against common threats and applied the lesson on a grand scale: the founding of the Camarilla in 1450. Alongside creating the sect, Hardestadt recreated Camilla's ancient council of peers, chartering roughly two dozen respected Ventrue as the Council of Ephors (also called directors) to counsel the clan and adjudicate grievances — their identities kept secret so no single personality could overshadow the council's authority. This body persists into the modern nights as the Ventrue Directorate.

pages.name: Philippe de Margaux, the Returned Strategos

text.content: Embraced in A.D. 894, Philippe de Margaux rose to become a Ventrue prince on two separate occasions and served nearly three decades as an archon before achieving the clan honorific of strategos, the second-highest accolade the Ventrue recognize. A strong candidate for justicar, he vanished mysteriously in 1791 on his way to a Directorate convocation in Lyons and was presumed destroyed by the Sabbat — only to reappear from centuries of torpor in the modern nights. Stripped of his old resources and struggling to grasp a world transformed beyond recognition, Philippe now trades on his surviving dignitas and rank, playing rival factions of young Ventrue against one another as each hopes his endorsement (and reputation) will further their own ambitions.

A German-born childe of the Inquisition years and one of the Camarilla's first archons, Robert Kross was the first Ventrue to grasp the potential of investing in the new mercantile ventures of the Renaissance, settling in Holland as a silent partner in trade with the Far East and amassing vast wealth for himself and his sire's cause. His childe Juan-Miguel Ramirez repeated the trick in Spain. Kross later relocated to the United States during the interwar Depression years, helping the American Ventrue check the first successful anarch revolt on the West Coast. He remains active in the modern nights, among those elders now searching for the lost Camilla and Lysander in hopes of resolving the clan's directionless drift under the secretive Directorate.

pages.name: The Feud of Massilia and Ravenna

text.content: One of the clan's most infamous rivalries: Demetrius, Prince of Massilia (Marseilles) for centuries since the city's Greek founding, blamed the elder Ventrue Gaius Fabricius of Ravenna for failing to prevent Rome's first-century B.C. conquest of his beloved free city — even though Julius Caesar, not Fabricius, bore actual responsibility. Fabricius, weary of Demetrius' unrelenting attacks, eventually took up the feud in earnest. Two thousand years later, both reputed to be of the fifth generation, the two elders still work against one another at every turn, sometimes taking their aggression out on unsuspecting neonates who merely share a rival's bloodline. Their grudge stands as a cautionary tale that not every move in the Jyhad is grave — some are simply petty, fueled by millennia of bitterness.

Founded by Hardestadt the Elder in 1450 alongside the Camarilla itself, the Council of Ephors — better known tonight as the Ventrue Directorate — is a body of roughly two dozen respected or influential Ventrue who counsel individual clan members and provide a forum for grievances, in theory free of regional bias. By long agreement, each ephor (or director) keeps his identity secret, so that no single personality can overshadow the council's collective authority. In the modern nights the Directorate has grown increasingly secretive and, according to its critics, does as much to foment unrest and justify its own existence as it does to lead; it has, however, taken direct action on matters such as monitoring nuclear proliferation through an informal clique of "watchers," and some Ventrue suspect that the long-vanished Camilla and Lysander may themselves sit unrevealed among its ranks.
